prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Personalize Your New Desktop Pet", "Give your pet a name"]
1: ["How to Control Your Desktop Pet", "Click your pet to chat, right-click to hide or open settings, and drag them anywhere on your desktop screen."]
2: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion Story", "Select how you want your desktop pet companion to assist your daily workflow.", "Select Companion Role"]
3: []
4: ["Setting up your pet desktop environment. This takes just a moment.", "Fun pet facts while you wait"]
5: ["Choose Your Pet Companion", "Includes Free Companion Starter Pack"]
6: ["Your Pet is Live on Your Desktop!", "Look at the corner of your screen. Click your pet to chat, or right-click anytime to open controls.", "Say Hello to Your Pet"]
7: ["Choose Your Companion's Specialty", "Select a focus mode, play companion, or relaxing background companion."]
8: ["Signing in secures your pet creation so it will never reset or be lost.", "Automatic Cloud Save Enabled"]
9: ["Initializing desktop pet renderer..."]
